args.text: When a process description presents mutually exclusive outcomes that each conclude with a different activity, model the branches as converging to a shared end event rather than giving each branch a separate end event.

trace.reason: Check whether existing documented guidance already covers merging alternative branches into a common process ending.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.

args.text: When mutually exclusive branches represent alternative outcomes of the same process, determine whether they share a process completion state; if so, merge them before a shared end event instead of adding a separate end event for each branch.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers the shared-end structure implicated by the extra end event and flows.

result.rule: When the description presents alternatives for one part of a process while requiring other work to be completed before a later activity: Model the alternatives with an exclusive gateway and the required work as parallel branches; synchronize the required branches before the later activity that depends on their completion.

When the description states that a process can end in two or more mutually exclusive outcomes: Model each outcome on its own branch from a decision gateway, connecting that branch to the corresponding outcome activity or end event.

When the description says that items are processed in turn, an overall completion condition is checked, and another item is selected for processing if the condition is not met: Model the completion check as an exclusive split: route the unmet-condition path through next-item selection and back to item processing, and route the met-condition path onward. Converge the initial entry and repeat path at the item-processing entry with an exclusive merge gateway.

When the description states how the process ends or gives a conditional branch without stating that the branch terminates the process: Label an end event only with an outcome explicitly stated for process termination; do not assign it an inferred or unstated branch outcome.
